title: Token Power Grid
blurb: Every word an AI writes burns energy. Run a city's AI on a tight token budget without a blackout.
objectives: What tokens are and why they cost energy
How to match an answer's length to what's actually needed

glossary.def: A small chunk of text (about a word piece). AIs read and write in tokens.
The computer work an AI does. More tokens = more compute = more energy.
A limit on how many tokens you can spend.
Getting the most helpfulness out of the fewest tokens.

steps.title: The city runs on tokens
steps.body:
A futuristic city powers all its AI helpers from one energy grid. Every time an AI generates text, it uses **tokens** — and tokens take **computation**, which takes **energy**.

More words → more tokens → more power drawn. The city engineer needs you: keep the AI helpful **and** keep the lights on.

steps.title: Short vs long
steps.prompt: Which answer costs the grid more energy?
choices: A long, detailed reply with extra examples
steps.afterPick: The long one — more tokens, more compute, more energy. Detail is great, but only when it's actually needed. Let's manage a real budget. →

steps.title: Answer the city within budget
steps.youWillDo: answer every request without blowing the token budget
steps.body: Each citizen request is **simple** or **needs detail**. Pick a reply length for each — but watch the **token meter**. Spend detail where it helps, keep simple asks short, and stay under budget. Go over and the grid browns out!

steps.title: Match the length to the need
steps.body:
The trick wasn't “always short” or “always long.” It was **matching the reply to the request**: short answers for simple questions, detail only where it genuinely helped.

That's efficiency — the most help for the fewest tokens. At the scale of millions of requests, it's the difference between a stable grid and a blackout.

steps.title: Why does length matter?
steps.question: Why does a longer AI answer cost more to produce?
choices: Each extra token is extra computation, which uses more energy
steps.explain: Every token is real compute. More tokens = more energy and cost — which is why efficient prompting and answers matter at scale.

steps.title: Say it your way
steps.prompt: Why is it smart to ask an AI for a short answer when a short answer is all you need?
steps.placeholder: Because every word the AI writes…

recall.question: Using fewer tokens (when you can) mainly helps by…
recall.explain: Fewer tokens → less compute → less energy and cost, with the same usefulness.

steps.title: Efficient AI 🎉
steps.body:
You learned something most people never think about: AI has a **real running cost**. The huge models you use run in **data centers** that draw serious electricity.

Good AI design isn't just about being smart — it's about being **efficient**: helpful answers, fewer wasted tokens. **Next up:** put it all together and run a whole AI product, start to finish.
